subject.title: fix(core): surface non_deliverable_terminal_turn as outbound fallback to channel plugins

question: Should `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` bypass `message_tool_only` suppression as an automatic core fallback, or should OpenClaw expose a plugin-owned terminal-failure hook instead?
rationale: Both options change the user-visible channel contract, and the linked canonical issue already has protected ClawSweeper labels asking for maintainer/product direction before new fix PRs proceed.

options.title: Approve core fallback exception
options.body: Land a narrow, tested exception that sends a safe failure notice only for confirmed non-deliverable terminal turns.

options.title: Use a plugin SDK hook
options.body: Add and document a terminal-failure hook so each channel plugin owns its fallback delivery behavior.

options.title: Keep message-tool-only strict
options.body: Reject automatic fallback delivery and leave channel plugins to handle non-deliverable turns through existing plugin-owned paths.

recommendation.title: Approve core fallback exception
recommendation.body: Land a narrow, tested exception that sends a safe failure notice only for confirmed non-deliverable terminal turns.

likelyOwner.reason: The current suppression gates and terminal classifier blame to recent Vincent Koc work, and adjacent commits connect him to silent-turn and plugin outbound routing behavior.
